summary: Front Psychol 2024 (secondary analysis, n=47): outcome expectations to hypnosis were NOT associated with perceived stress reduction at 5 weeks (B=0.326, p=0.812). Suggests hypnosis effect not driven by expectancy in this sample — partial support for hypnosis-specific mechanisms.
content: Front Psychol 2024, 'The relevance of outcome expectations in group hypnosis for stress reduction' (secondary analysis of multicenter RCT, n=47 distressed participants). Group hypnosis program 5 weekly sessions + audio + educational booklet. Outcome expectations measured at baseline with Expectations for Treatment Scale (ETS). RESULT: unadjusted (B=0.326, p=0.812, R2=0.001) and adjusted (B=0.639, p=0.641, R2=0.168) regressions found outcome expectations to hypnosis were NOT associated with change in perceived stress between baseline and 5 weeks in the intervention group. CONCLUSION: 'beneficial effect of group hypnosis in distressed participants were not associated with outcome expectations. Other mechanisms of action may be more important for the effect of hypnosis.' Caveats: ceiling on expectations (M=13.74/20); single-arm (intervention only); ETS developed for acupuncture. KEY: partial support for hypnosis-SPECIFIC effects beyond expectancy — counterbalances EV-0033's large placebo component and EV-0034's induction-null finding.
